claim_text: 來源機構：Smart Learning Environments (Springer Nature)；資料標題：Student epistemic agency in AI-mediated practices；來源刊登日：2026-10-24。作者摘要報告：研究在一所已啟動「AI 排入課表」試辦計畫的瑞典學校進行，對象為國家課綱未納入 AI 教學的義務教育學生；向 47 名七年級學生發放涵蓋來源評估、資料隱私、演算法操弄、透明、責任與治理等面向的問卷，並以題目配對交叉表分析；作者報告學生在部分面向展現強的認知能動性，但在資料隱私與演算法操弄等其他面向能動性弱，即使這些內容先前已納入教學。（AI 輔助摘要，未經真人逐則審稿；請參閱原文。）
source_title: Student epistemic agency in AI-mediated practices
title_zh: AI 中介實踐中的學生認知能動性
source_locator: 出版社文章頁（SpringerOpen，2026-10-26 讀取 200）：Published 24 October 2026，citation_online_date 2026/10/24，Crossref published-online 同日；Received 23 June 2026、Accepted 29 August 2026；摘要歸屬：Abstract 第 2 至 4 句、第 6 句
original_excerpt: This study was conducted in a Swedish school that had started the pilot project “AI on the schedule” for compulsory school students, for whom the national curricula do not include AI training. … A survey covering the aspects of source evaluation, data privacy, algorithmic manipulation, transparency, responsibility, and governance was distributed to these year 7 students (n = 47). … The data was analysed through cross-tabulations of question pairs. … Results show that students demonstrated strong epistemic agency in certain areas but weak agency in others, for example, in data privacy and algorithmic manipulation, even when these had been part of earlier instruction.
interpretation_note: 轉述作者摘要的研究場域、對象、問卷面向、分析方法與作者報告的描述性結果；屬單一學校的描述性調查，不涉及介入成效。

summary_evidence_spans: This study was conducted in a Swedish school that had started the pilot project “AI on the schedule” for compulsory school students, for whom the national curricula do not include AI training.
A survey covering the aspects of source evaluation, data privacy, algorithmic manipulation, transparency, responsibility, and governance was distributed to these year 7 students (n = 47).
The data was analysed through cross-tabulations of question pairs.

Results show that students demonstrated strong epistemic agency in certain areas but weak agency in others, for example, in data privacy and algorithmic manipulation, even when these had been part of earlier instruction.
